As a 110 lbs woman mace would be quite effective. I've seen 200 lbs 6 ft+ men just walk off mace to the face. Bear mace might be a different story, but this weak "self-defense" mace is not reliable. It's mostly meant for stopping large dogs at best.

If you shoot someone with a .22 or if you shoot them in something like the arm then yes you are correct. If you shoot someone with a shotgun, or a .45 handgun and you shoot them somewhere more critical you are correct. To me the main feature of a firearm is that it will make an assailant hesitate. People know guns, when used effectively, can kill. A smart person would yield to that.

I'm 230 lbs and 6 ft and have been sprayed with mace for testing and it was not pleasant, that is the reaction was instant. In fact just letting off a single spray in closed off room by mistake was enough to empty the room due to gagging issues. I'm thinking that if someone is that far gone where they can "walk off" the effects of mace - which I suppose is possible - then they're not going to be of any sort of a rational mindset to actually be intimidated via a gun. I dunno, the best argument I can give is just to try the stuff on yourself and see what happens.

Also, as an aside to the point you made, even if they are of a rational mindset then it's possible that they will simply call your bluff because they know that your only option is lethal force. For example there have been cases where someone has had a gun drawn on them and they have simply reloaded their own weapon and shot whoever had the gun drawn on them due to the others inability to act. It's one thing to make a threat of violence but such a threat is worthless if you having nothing to back that original threat up. This is especially true when one party is rational with things to lose while the other is a lunatic with nothing.

As for your second point, current police procedure in the US is to shoot two rounds at the mid-section of a knife wielding assailant when at a distance of 22 feet, or 7 meters. And even this has been argued to be too close. My argument isn't that a shot wouldn't kill them more that even if it did then there is still more than enough momentum for them to do damage. Granted there are many factors as play such as the distance to the target or the calibre of weapon etc, as you have correctly pointed out. But I think that because this has become the standard protocol when the police are facing off against guys with knifes, says it all really, as too the effectiveness of these weapons.

What type of mace though? There are many different concentrations as I mentioned. Bear mace would certainly stop a grown man because as the name implies it is intended to stop a goddamn bear. However that type of mace is much different from the kind marketed as self defense mace. As a matter of fact I have accidentally sprayed myself with the self defense mace (usually equivalent in potency to dog mace) as a teenager and it was not much more than bearable pain and teary eyes. It certainly did nothing to incapacitate me physically.

Of course you'd have to be willing to kill or seriously injure someone; but the argument of "bluffing" applies to any weapon. Take a baseball bat for example. Whipping one out in defense will do you no good if you aren't willing to do some serious damage with it.

As for your third point, the fact that I specifically mentioned .22 caliber weapons as basically ineffective explains my feelings about this. A .22 is a poor choice for a self defense weapon IMO. It might suffice for the police but they are under much different circumstances than a solitary private citizen under attack. If you instead had a .45 handgun or 7.62 rifle and you are a decent shot you should have no problem incapacitating someone. If you genuinely felt that you or someone else was in serious danger you do not really have an option anyway. Personally I wouldn't even worry about if the amount of force I was using was too much because I'd rather be facing charges for excessive force than be dead or raped.
